info.name: CRM Lite
info.description: CRM Lite backend API collection. Import together with CRM-Lite.local.postman_environment.json and read docs/postman/README.md for startup order, execution order and how dynamic variables are populated. AUTHENTICATION (ADR-006..008): every business request through the gateway needs a logged-in BFF session (Authorization Code + PKCE via the browser — see folder 09 and the README §Authentication). Direct Grant/ROPC is disabled by design; never store passwords or tokens in this collection.

item.name: 09 - Authentication (session probe and logout)
item.description: The gateway is a cookie-session BFF (ADR-007): it does NOT accept Authorization: Bearer. Log in once via the BROWSER (http://localhost:8080/api/session/me -> Keycloak login ayilmaz/crm-dev), then copy the JSESSIONID and XSRF-TOKEN cookie values from browser devtools into Postman: Cookies (below the Send button) -> Add domain localhost -> add both cookies for port 8080. Postman then sends them automatically; set the xsrfToken environment variable to the XSRF-TOKEN value for unsafe requests (folders 04/05/06 write operations). Full contract: docs/api/authentication.md.

request.description: RP-initiated logout (ADR-007/008): kills the gateway session synchronously and returns 200 with {logoutUrl} — Keycloak's end_session endpoint. A GET to logoutUrl completes the Keycloak SSO logout and lands on Keycloak's sign-in form, since post_logout_redirect_uri is the gateway's /oauth2/authorization/keycloak (the app does this via window.location.replace, after the user confirms the sign-out dialog; this request alone only ends the gateway session). item.name: 12 - Asynchronous SALE (FR-SALE, ADR-018)
item.description:
The LIVE sale flow: draft -> 202 submit -> poll. Requires the services to run with SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=async-sale and the Compose 'eventing' profile up; without them the submit request answers 503 MSG-SERVICE-UNAVAILABLE by design (fail closed rather than accepting a sale nothing can process).

Run the requests in order — each stores what the next one needs (draftOrderNumber, submitOrderNumber, abandonOrderNumber). Idempotency-Key values are minted per request with {{$guid}} except where a test deliberately reuses one.

The deprecated synchronous POST /api/orders is NOT exercised here: one sale must never enter both routes, and the async submit refuses any order that is not a WAIT draft.

request.description:
No accountNumber in the body — it is read from the draft, so a basket built against a different account cannot be re-pointed. One order_db transaction writes the items, moves WAIT -> MIDLWARE, creates the saga row and records its first Outbox command; the 202 is returned after that commit.

If this answers 503 MSG-SERVICE-UNAVAILABLE, the services are not running with SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=async-sale. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour, not a bug.

item.name: Submit the SAME order again with a NEW key -> 409 MSG-ORDER-NOT-DRAFT

request.description: A new key bypasses the idempotency replay, so this reaches the service — and is refused because the order is no longer WAIT. This is the same guard that makes it impossible for one sale to enter both the legacy synchronous route and this one: a legacy order is created MIDLWARE and can therefore never be submitted here.

item.name: Cancel before submit: create a second draft

request.description: A draft that will be abandoned rather than submitted.

WAIT only, and idempotent — send it twice and both answer 204, because a client that lost the response must be able to ask again. No Idempotency-Key: DELETE of a named resource is idempotent by identity.

This is NOT an order-cancellation feature: a submitted (MIDLWARE) order is refused with 409, which is what keeps the KR-7 cancellation out of scope.

request.description: The public contract has four processing values, so an abandoned draft reports FAILED and distinguishes itself through failureMessageKey. It keeps its KR-12 number forever — a compensated or abandoned order is a record of something that was attempted, not something that never happened.
